title: VLSI Design and Experimental Demonstration of Photonic Interposers in Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
problem: Optimizing photonic interposer performance requires accounting for optical timing skew, propagation loss, routing/placement blockages, and seamless integration with EDA tools—challenges for which mature design automation does not exist.
motivation: Enable energy-efficient clock distribution and high-bandwidth communication among chiplets via photonic interposers with mature EDA tool integration.
method: They convert photonic designs to electronic form, optimize them with standard chip-design software, and convert back to photonic layouts—reusing proven design methods. They apply this to design an optical clock tree (distributing light-based timing) and optical router (directing light signals), then fabricate and test a photonic interposer in thin-film lithium niobate.
key_novelty: This is the first transformation that lets standard chip-design tools optimize photonic circuits, demonstrated by building a photonic interposer in thin-film lithium niobate.
contributions: 13.85% optical timing skew improvement vs standalone OCT design tools
128x128 electro-optical router design automation in <40 minutes
2.16 dB optical loss skew measured experimentally
Phase-adaptive optical power modulation for loss reduction

metrics.other: 2.16 dB loss skew (experimental), 40 min design time for 128x128 router

baselines: Standalone optical clock tree design tools
limitations: Experimental demonstration limited to specific TFLN configurations; high-level design automation results on representative examples.
primary_theme: EDA-compatible photonic interposer design and TFLN experimental demonstration
